The text uses one temperature value, the arithmetic uses a different one; this is an internal inconsistency. Either the measurement was made at 318.15 K (in which case the text should say so) or the calculation was performed with the wrong temperature (in which case the activation energy is wrong). The discrepancy is evident in the sentence:  
“*… at 318 K gives k = 1.28 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹, and applying the Arrhenius relation … at 298.15 K and 318.15 K …*”

FOLLOW: The activation energy derived from the Arrhenius relation is fed into the storage‑temperature sensitivity of the hold‑time model (Section 9). If the 318 K measurement were the true condition, the correct activation energy would be ∼75.8 kJ mol⁻¹, not 75.2 kJ mol⁻¹. This would alter the predicted degradation rate at other temperatures and could mis‑size the wet‑cake hold schedule, potentially leading to product that deviates from specification when stored even slightly off‑nominal. The downstream dependency chain is CH‑35 → hold‑time model → batch release criteria.

ANALYSE: HARD. Consistency of stated measurement conditions with the numbers derived from them is a physical‑measurement constraint. The document internally contradicts itself. Classification: **CONFIRMED** (the inconsistency is present in the text).

FIX: The simplest sufficient correction is to align the descriptive text with the computation. Because the computation already uses 318.15 K (and is arithmetically consistent with that value), the text should read “at 318.15 K”.
